title: Acute Coronary Syndrome: ECG, Troponin and Risk Assessment
subject: Medicine
preview: Acute coronary syndrome includes unstable angina, NSTEMI and STEMI, with differences in ECG and myocardial injury evidence.
quickRevision: Acute coronary syndrome includes unstable angina, NSTEMI and STEMI, with differences in ECG and myocardial injury evidence.
Time-sensitive reperfusion pathways apply to suitable STEMI patterns; alternatives such as aortic dissection remain important in atypical cases.
Antiplatelet and anticoagulant decisions depend on diagnosis, bleeding risk and local pathways.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Acute coronary syndrome includes unstable angina, NSTEMI and STEMI, with differences in ECG and myocardial injury evidence.
Serial ECG and high-sensitivity troponin measurements help evaluate an evolving presentation.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Time-sensitive reperfusion pathways apply to suitable STEMI patterns; alternatives such as aortic dissection remain important in atypical cases.
Antiplatelet and anticoagulant decisions depend on diagnosis, bleeding risk and local pathways.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A single normal early troponin does not exclude a developing acute coronary syndrome.

quiz.question: Which marker is used to detect acute myocardial injury in ACS evaluation?
quiz.explanation: Cardiac troponin. A single normal early troponin does not exclude a developing acute coronary syndrome.
